cna.title: Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below is vulnerable to CSRF on download() in the package install controller

descriptions.value: CAPEC-467 Cross Site Identification

Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below does not validate a CSRF token before processing requests to /dashboard/extend/install/download/<remoteId>. The download() method in concrete/controllers/single_page/dashboard/extend/install.php checks only the canInstallPackages() permission before fetching a remote marketplace package and writing it to the server's DIR_PACKAGES directory. Because the endpoint is a state-changing GET route with no token enforcement, an attacker who can cause an authenticated administrator to visit a crafted page can force an arbitrary marketplace package to be downloaded. In order to be vulnerable, the victim must be passing canInstallPackages() and the site must be connected to the Concrete marketplace. The Concrete CMS security team gave this vulnerability a CVSS v.4.0 score of 7.5 with vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. Thanks  https://github.com/maru1009  for reporting.

cna.title: Unbounded buffer accumulation in multipart header parsing causes denial of service in plug

descriptions.value: CAPEC-130 Excessive Allocation

references.name: Unbounded buffer accumulation in multipart header parsing causes denial of service in Plug

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in plug_project plug allows denial of service via unbounded buffer accumulation in multipart header parsing.

Plug.Conn.read_part_headers/2 in lib/plug/conn.ex does not obey its :length parameter. There is no upper bound on the size of the accumulated buffer. By contrast, the sibling function read_part_body has an explicit byte_size(acc) > length guard that stops accumulation once a limit is reached. No such guard exists in read_part_headers. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server memory by sending a crafted multipart/form-data request, causing a denial of service.

This issue affects plug: from 1.4.0-rc.0 before 1.15.4, from 1.16.0 before 1.16.3, from 1.17.0 before 1.17.1, from 1.18.0 before 1.18.2, and from 1.19.0 before 1.19.2.

cna.title: WP-Ultimate-Map <= 1.1 - Cross-Site Request Forgery to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'zoom-level' Parameter

descriptions.value: The WP-Ultimate-Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 1.1. This is due to missing nonce validation on the process_init() function hooked to admin_init, which saves plugin settings (zoom-level, focus-lat, focus-lng, sel_places, sel_routes) via update_option() based solely on the presence of a save-setting POST parameter. Additionally, the saved values — particularly zoom-level — are stored without sanitization and later echoed into an HTML attribute (and inline JavaScript) on the settings page without escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to change plugin settings and inject arbitrary web scripts via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link.

cna.title: ClearSale Total <= 3.4.2 - Unauthenticated SQL Injection

descriptions.value: The ClearSale Total plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the `pagseguro[metodo]` POST parameter of the `clearsale_total_push` AJAX action in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.2. The handler is registered for unauthenticated users (`wp_ajax_nopriv_clearsale_total_push`), and although a `wp_verify_nonce()` check exists, the failing branch's `die()` is commented out so execution continues regardless of nonce validity. On PHP < 8.0 the attacker-supplied `$metodo` value bypasses the `switch ($metodo) { case 4: ... }` guard via loose type juggling (the string `"4 AND SLEEP(5)"` compares equal to integer `4`), reaching an unquoted `UPDATE wp_cs_total_dadosextras SET metodo=$metodo, ...` query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires the target server to be running PHP < 8.0.

cna.title: justhtml before 1.12.0 Sanitizer Bypass via Markdown

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: justhtml before 1.12.0 Sanitizer Bypass via Markdown

descriptions.value: justhtml versions <= 1.11.0 (fixed in 1.12.0) do not sufficiently escape HTML-significant characters (angle brackets) in text nodes when converting a parsed document to Markdown via to_markdown(). While a small set of Markdown metacharacters are escaped, characters such as < and > are preserved, so untrusted input that is safe in to_html() — including entity-decoded text (e.g. <script>) or text from RCDATA/RAWTEXT-parsed elements like <title>, <textarea>, <noscript>, and <plaintext> — can be emitted as raw HTML in the Markdown output, enabling a sanitizer bypass and potential cross-site scripting when that output is rendered.

descriptions.value: A vulnerability has been identified in LibreOffice Calc. An application crash may occur if a user opens a malicious spreadsheet that contains excessively long formulas. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could result in a denial of service or potentially lead to arbitrary code execution.

cna.title: Heap buffer overflow in Calc formula compilation

credits.value: Arthur Chan of Ada Logics (validation and reporting)

descriptions.value: CAPEC-44 Overflow Binary Resource File

LibreOffice Calc compiles cell formulas when opening a spreadsheet. A heap buffer overflow existed when compiling a very long formula made up of many opening tokens. The array that tracks nesting depth was allocated one element too small for that worst case, so such a formula wrote one element past its end. In fixed versions the array is sized to hold the largest possible nesting.

In fixed versions the array is sized to hold the largest possible nesting.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-179 Calling Micro-Services Directly

Impact

A security issue has been identified in Chef 360 that could allow unauthorized access to protected API endpoints under specific conditions. This issue is due to improper handling of URL-encoded paths during request processing. In certain scenarios, an authenticated request may bypass standard access controls gaining additional privileges, potentially allowing access to API endpoints that are intended to be restricted to higher-permissioned roles. The impact is limited to environments where the affected request patterns can be triggered and depends on specific deployment configuration and access controls in place.
Resolution
The issue has been addressed through product updates that improve request validation and enforce strict path normalization before authorization checks.  Customers are advised to update to the latest available version containing the fix, version 1.7.1 or later.

cna.title: radare2 6.1.5 Use-After-Free via gdbr_pids_list()

descriptions.value: radare2 6.1.5 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the gdbr_pids_list() function within the GDB client core that allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code by sending malformed thread information responses. credits.value: Arthur Chan of Ada Logics (validation and reporting)

descriptions.value: CAPEC-44 Overflow Binary Resource File

LibreOffice Calc can import tracked changes from a spreadsheet document. A heap buffer overflow existed when a document reused the same change identifier for two different kinds of change. The importer then treated one change object as a different, larger type and wrote past the end of its allocation. In fixed versions records with a duplicate identifier are rejected.

cna.title: Relative Path Traversal in allegroai/clearml

descriptions.value: A vulnerability in allegroai/clearml versions up to and including 1.16.5 allows for relative path traversal when extracting `.zip` archives using the `ZipFile.extractall()` method in `StorageManager._extract_to_cache()`. This issue arises due to the lack of path traversal validation, enabling an attacker to write arbitrary files to the filesystem. Attack vectors include dataset downloads, artifact downloads, model downloads, and offline session imports. The vulnerability can lead to remote code execution through methods such as cron job injection, SSH key overwrite, or web shell deployment. The issue is resolved in version 2.1.6.

solutions.value: Users of potentially infected application are recommended to uninstall the application, run a full system scan using antivirus software with the latest version of the anti-virus databases, and install the latest version of DAEMON Tools Lite (12.6 or newer) from the official website.

references.name: DAEMON Tools software infected – supply chain attack ongoing since April 8, 2026
Security Incident Affecting DAEMON Tools Lite: What We Know So Far

descriptions.value: A supply chain attack compromised the official installation packages of DAEMON Tools Lite (Windows versions 12.5.0.2421 through 12.5.0.2434), distributed from the legitimate website daemon-tools.cc between approximately April 8, 2026, and May 5, 2026. Attackers gained unauthorized access to the vendor's (AVB Disc Soft) build or distribution infrastructure and trojanized three binaries: DTHelper.exe, DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe, and DTShellHlp.exe. These files were digitally signed with the legitimate AVB Disc Soft code-signing certificate, allowing the malicious installers to appear trustworthy and bypass signature-based detection.

This is due to insufficient access controls on the 'ays_poll_get_user_information' AJAX action, which serializes and returns the complete WP_User object — including the user_pass (bcrypt password hash), user_email, user_login, user_registered, roles, and all capabilities — without any nonce verification or capability check beyond is_user_logged_in(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to retrieve sensitive account data including their own password hash, which WordPress does not expose through any of its standard interfaces and which can be leveraged for offline password-cracking attacks.

descriptions.description: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

cna.title: Login with OTP <= 1.6 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via OTP Brute Force

descriptions.value: The Login with OTP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authentication bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.6. This is due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-11178: the rate-limit/lockout check added to `otpl_login_action()` was placed only inside the OTP-generation branch and is never evaluated on the OTP-validation branch, and the generated 6-digit OTP additionally has no expiration. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to brute-force the 900,000-value OTP space for any user account (including administrators) and obtain a valid `wp_set_auth_cookie()` session, leading to full site compromise.

descriptions.description: CWE-307 Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

descriptions.value: The WP GDPR Cookie Consent plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'ninja_gdpr_ajax_actions' AJAX action in versions up to, and including, 1.0.0. This is due to missing capability and nonce checks on the handleAjaxCalls() function, combined with insufficient input sanitization on the gdprConfig values and missing output escaping in the generateCSS() function which echoes stored configuration values directly into a <style> block rendered on wp_head. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

cna.title: Authorization Bypass in mlflow/mlflow

descriptions.value: In MLflow versions prior to 3.14.0, when running with authentication enabled, the trace API endpoints lack proper authorization validators. This allows any authenticated user to bypass experiment-level authorization controls on all trace operations, including reading, deleting, and modifying traces on experiments they do not have permission to access. The issue arises from the `_before_request` handler, which does not register authorization validators for trace endpoints, resulting in requests proceeding without validation. This vulnerability can expose sensitive data, destroy audit logs, and allow unauthorized modifications.

descriptions.value: The Booking calendar, Appointment Booking System plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.36. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to mark arbitrary reservations as paid or completed, cancel legitimate payments, auto-approve reservations, and trigger transactional booking emails by writing attacker-supplied payment status and transaction data directly into the payments table. The auto-approval of reservations is only triggered when the 'enable_psuccess_approval' site option is enabled, but payment status manipulation and email dispatch are exploitable regardless of that setting.

cna.title: Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below is vulnerable to CSRF on prepare_remote_upgrade() leading to one-request RCE via package overwrite

descriptions.value: CAPEC-657 Malicious Automated Software Update via Spoofing

Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below does not validate a CSRF token before processing requests to /dashboard/extend/update/prepare_remote_upgrade/<remoteMPID>. An attacker who controls the remote package returned for a known marketplace item ID can overwrite the package PHP on disk and force its upgrade() method to execute in a single browser navigation. This results in remote code execution as the web server user.   In order to be vulnerable, the victim must be passing canInstallPackages, victim site must be connected to the Concrete marketplace; and the attacker controls the package returned for a marketplace item ID already installed on the victim site. The Concrete CMS security team gave this vulnerability a CVSS v.4.0 score of 7.5 with vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. Thanks https://github.com/maru1009 for reporting.

cna.title: HTTP::Daemon versions before 6.17 for Perl allow OS command injection via send_file()

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Daemon 6.17 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Daemon versions before 6.17 for Perl allow OS command injection via send_file().

send_file() opens its string argument with Perl's 2-arg open(). The 2-arg form interprets magic prefixes: '| cmd' and 'cmd |' open a pipe to a subprocess, '> path' and '>> path' open the path for write or append.

Untrusted input passed to send_file() can run OS commands at the daemon process UID. The read-pipe form ('cmd |') also leaks subprocess stdout into the HTTP response body. The write-mode forms can create or truncate files at attacker chosen paths.

cna.title: Native entropy source retries the CPU entropy instructions without limit

affected.vendor: Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc.

descriptions.value: In Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bc-fips 2.1.3, the native entropy source used on Intel platforms retried the CPU entropy instructions without any bound. RDSEED and RDRAND report failure through their carry flag, and the JNI seeding routine spun re-issuing the instruction for as long as that flag stayed clear, so a persistent failure of the on-chip entropy source - whether from a hardware fault, from the underlying DRBG being exhausted by contention across many cores, or from a hypervisor that does not provide the instruction - left the calling thread looping indefinitely inside the JNI call, where it could be neither interrupted nor timed out. Any operation drawing from the native entropy source could therefore hang, denying service to the application. The retry loops are now bounded (200 attempts for RDSEED and 20 for RDRAND, twice the baselines given in Intel's Digital Random Number Generator software implementation guide), pausing between attempts and, on exhaustion, clearing any partially written buffer and throwing rather than continuing to spin. The clear is performed by an un-elidable memzero, which uses a volatile pointer and an assembly memory barrier so that a compiler cannot optimise the erase away as a dead store. Bouncy Castle for Java (bcprov) is not affected, as it has no native entropy source; the 1.0.X and 2.0.X FIPS series are not affected.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated user can bypass configured WebAuthn policies during credential registration by manipulating client-side JavaScript. cna.title: code100x Mobile API Authentication Bypass via Header Spoofing

descriptions.value: code100x contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the Mobile API that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate arbitrary users by supplying a crafted JSON payload in the 'g' HTTP header. cna.title: Games Catalog <= 1.2.0 - Cross-Site Request Forgery to Arbitrary Game/Post Deletion

descriptions.value: The Games Catalog plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 1.2.0. This is due to missing or incorrect nonce validation on the gc_crud() function which handles the delete action (action=delete) via a GET request without any wp_verify_nonce() / check_admin_referer() call. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary game catalog entries (including the associated WordPress post created for the game) via a forged request, granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link.

cna.title: Server-side request forgery vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server notebook viewer via URL parser confusion

descriptions.value: CAPEC-664 Server Side Request Forgery

A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability was identified in the GitHub Enterprise Server notebook viewer that allowed an attacker to access internal services by exploiting URL parser confusion between the validation layer and the HTTP request library. The hostname validation used a different URL parser than the request library, enabling a crafted URL to pass validation while directing the request to an unintended host. Exploitation required network access to the GitHub Enterprise Server instance. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.21 and was fixed in versions 3.16.18, 3.17.15, 3.18.9, 3.19.6, and 3.20.2. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

affected.product: Backup and Staging by WP Time Capsule

descriptions.value: The Backup and Staging by WP Time Capsule plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.22.26 via the download_recent_decrypted_file_wptc. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to extract download the most recently admin-decrypted SQL database backup, which typically contains password hashes, user credentials, and other sensitive site configuration data stored in the 'recent_decrypted_file' option. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously performed a decrypt action, causing the decrypted SQL backup file to exist in the plugin's upload directory; without this prior admin action, there is no file to serve.

cna.title: jQuery googleslides <= 1.3 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Shortcode Attributes

descriptions.value: The jQuery googleslides plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'googleslides' shortcode in all versions up to, and including, 1.3. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on user supplied attributes (userid, albumid, authkey, imgmax, maxresults, random, caption, albumlink, time, and fadespeed) in the googleslides_handler() function, which interpolates the attribute values directly into single-quoted HTML attributes without using esc_attr(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

workarounds.value: Where immediate upgrade is not feasible, customers should: (1) restrict CLI access to trusted administrators only; (2) enforce strong authentication and rotate any default credentials; (3) restrict physical access to serial console ports; and (4) monitor device logs for unexpected debug-mode activation attempts.

supportingMedia.value: Where immediate upgrade is not feasible, customers should: (1) restrict CLI access to trusted administrators only; (2) enforce strong authentication and rotate any default credentials; (3) restrict physical access to serial console ports; and (4) monitor device logs for unexpected debug-mode activation attempts.

descriptions.value:
ExtremeXOS (EXOS) uses a challenge-response mechanism to authorize access to the privileged debug-mode function. The challenge value is generated using an insufficiently random source, which under certain conditions may allow an attacker to predict the expected response and activate debug-mode without authorization. Depending on device configuration and version, this may enable escalation to root-level access and persistent modification of the device software stack. Exploitation requires either a valid low-privilege account on the device (remote scenario) or physical serial console access (local scenario). This vulnerability is distinct from CVE-2017-14329, which addressed a different issue involving Python script privileges.

cna.title: Apache::Session::Generate::SHA256 versions before 1.3.19 for Perl create insecure session ids

descriptions.value: CAPEC-115 Authentication Bypass
CAPEC-102 Session Sidejacking

workarounds.value: Upgrade to version 1.3.19 or later.

descriptions.value:
Apache::Session::Generate::SHA256 versions before 1.3.19 for Perl create insecure session ids.

Apache::Session::Generate::SHA256 generated session ids insecurely. The default session id generator returns a SHA-256 hash of the built-in rand() function, the epoch time, and the PID, that is hashed again. These are predictable, low-entropy sources. Predicable session ids could allow an attacker to gain access to systems.

Note that version 1.3.19 has a fallback without warning to use insecure session generation method if the call to Crypt::URandom::urandom fails. However, this is unlikely as Crypt::URandom is a hardcoded requirement of the module.

This issue is similar to CVE-2025-40931 for Apache::Session::Generate::MD5.

descriptions.description: CWE-340 Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers

cna.title: Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below is vulnerable to RCE due to insecure deserialization occurring in the ExpressEntryList block controller.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-116 Excavation
CAPEC-586 Object Injection

Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution  due to insecure deserialization occurring in the ExpressEntryList block controller. An rogue administrator with privileges to add blocks to an area can bypass the intended protection mechanism (_fromCIF === true), which normally restricts malicious inputs over form POST requests, by leveraging the REST API functionality. Because the REST API parses requests using json_decode(), the string "true" is evaluated as a strict PHP Boolean(true).  This bypass allows the attacker to inject a malicious serialized payload  into the block's filterFields database column. The payload will subsequently be executed when the block's data is viewed or edited by an administrator leading to complete server takeover (RCE).The Concrete CMS security team gave this vulnerability a CVSS v.4.0 score of 8.9 with a vector of CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:H/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H.  Thanks  Nguyễn Văn Thiện https://github.com/Thien225409  for reporting

cna.title: Google+ Link Name <= 1.0 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Shortcode Attributes

descriptions.value: The Google+ Link Name plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'gplusnamelink' shortcode in versions up to, and including, 1.0. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on user supplied attributes ('id' and 'name') in the gplusnamelink_generate() function, which are concatenated directly into the rendered HTML without calling esc_attr() or esc_html(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

cna.title: Login with NEAR <= 0.3.3 - Authentication Bypass via 'account' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Login with NEAR plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 0.3.3. The `ajaxLoginWithNear()` function — registered as a `wp_ajax_nopriv` action and therefore reachable by unauthenticated users — accepts an attacker-supplied `account` POST parameter and issues a valid WordPress authentication cookie based solely on a substring check for `.near`, with no nonce verification, cryptographic signature validation, challenge-response exchange, or any proof that the requester controls the corresponding NEAR wallet. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress user, including administrators, whose email address matches the deterministic `<account>@near.org` pattern derived from the supplied `account` value. If no matching user exists, the handler automatically creates and authenticates a new WordPress account for the attacker-controlled identifier, providing a further avenue for unauthorized account creation.

cna.title: WWW::Mechanize::Cached versions before 2.00 for Perl deserialize cached HTTP responses from a world-writable on-disk cache, enabling local response forgery and code execution

solutions.value: Upgrade to WWW-Mechanize-Cached 2.00 or later.

descriptions.value:
WWW::Mechanize::Cached versions before 2.00 for Perl deserialize cached HTTP responses from a world-writable on-disk cache, enabling local response forgery and code execution.

With no explicit cache backend, WWW::Mechanize::Cached constructs a default Cache::FileCache under /tmp/FileCache without overriding the backend's documented directory_umask of 000, so the cache root and its subdirectories are created mode 0777 with no sticky bit. Cache entries are named by sha1_hex of the request and read back through Storable::thaw on the next cache hit.

A local attacker with write access to the cache tree can replace a victim's cache entry for a known URL with an arbitrary frozen HTTP::Response blob, causing the victim's next get() of that URL to return attacker controlled response bytes. Because the bytes are passed to Storable::thaw, a victim process that has loaded any class with a side-effectful STORABLE_thaw, DESTROY, or overload hook can be escalated to arbitrary code execution.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-242 Code Injection

references.name: Unauthenticated remote code execution via HEEx template injection in phoenix_storybook playground

descriptions.value:
Code Injection vulnerability in phenixdigital phoenix_storybook allows unauthenticated remote code execution via HEEx template injection in the component playground. A client can send attribute values over the playground WebSocket. A value that closes the attribute quote and adds a HEEx expression is evaluated as Elixir code on the server.

PhoenixStorybook.Story.PlaygroundPreviewLive.handle_event/3 accepts attribute names and values from the client and stores them through PhoenixStorybook.ExtraAssignsHelpers.handle_set_variation_assign/3. PhoenixStorybook.Rendering.ComponentRenderer.attributes_markup/1 interpolates string values into a HEEx template without escaping. The template is compiled with EEx.compile_string/2 and evaluated. Releases published as phx_live_storybook have the same code in the PhxLiveStorybook namespace, where the first client entry point is PhxLiveStorybook.Entry.Playground.handle_event/3.

This issue affects phoenix_storybook: from 0.5.0 before 1.1.0; phx_live_storybook: from 0.3.0 onward.

cna.title: MapPress Maps for WordPress <= 2.96.6 - Unauthenticated Insecure Direct Object Reference via REST API Endpoints

descriptions.value: The MapPress Maps for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key in all versions up to, and including, 2.96.6. This is due to missing ownership verification in the REST API routes registered via `Mappress_Api::rest_api_init()`, where the GET `/wp-json/mapp/v1/maps/{mapid}` endpoint uses `'permission_callback' => '__return_true'` and the write endpoints (POST update, DELETE, PATCH mutate, POST clone, POST empty_trash) only check the generic `edit_posts` capability without confirming that the requester owns the targeted map — a gap that is not compensated at the model layer, as `Mappress_Map::get()`, `save()`, `delete()`, `mutate()`, and `empty_trash()` all operate on any caller-supplied map ID without an ownership check. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive map data — including POI titles, addresses, coordinates, and body content — for any map on the site by enumerating map IDs, and for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to modify, delete, trash/restore, or clone any map regardless of its author.

cna.title: Path traversal in Zephyr HTTP server static-filesystem resource handler allows unauthenticated remote arbitrary file read

descriptions.value: Zephyr's HTTP server (subsys/net/lib/http) provides a static-filesystem resource type (HTTP_RESOURCE_TYPE_STATIC_FS, available when CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM is enabled) that serves files from a configured root directory. Before this fix, both the HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 front-ends placed the raw, attacker-controlled request path into client->url_buffer (assembled in on_url() for HTTP/1 and copied verbatim from the :path pseudo-header for HTTP/2) without resolving ./.. segments. The static-FS handler then built the on-disk filename by directly concatenating the configured root with that raw URL (snprintk(fname, ..., "%s%s", static_fs_detail->fs_path, client->url_buffer) at http_server_http1.c:603 and http_server_http2.c:490) and opened it with fs_open(fname, FS_O_READ). Because the handler is reached via wildcard/leading-dir (fnmatch FNM_LEADING_DIR) or fallback resource matching, a request such as GET /<prefix>/../../<file> is dispatched to the handler and, after the underlying filesystem (e.g. LittleFS/FAT) resolves the .. segments, escapes the configured web root, letting an unauthenticated remote client read arbitrary readable files on the mounted volume (information disclosure). The HTTP server requires no TLS or authentication to reach this path. The fix adds http_server_remove_dot_segments(), which canonicalizes the path portion of the URL before resource lookup in both protocol handlers, neutralizing the traversal. Affects releases v4.0.0 through v4.4.0 for deployments that register a static-filesystem resource.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv.

Unless it is short plain ASCII, a quoted key is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

cna.title: Busybox: httpd password rule bypass for pre-compressed .gz files via accept-encoding: gzip

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Duc Anh Luu for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
To mitigate this vulnerability without modifying binary features, apply one of the following configuration measures:

1. Configure directory-level authentication:
In the BusyBox `httpd.conf` configuration file, define authentication rules covering the containing directory rather than individual file paths. Directory rules are evaluated against both the base request and served compressed variants.

2. Protect base filenames:
When individual file protection is necessary, configure password rules for both the uncompressed filename and the `.gz` filename (for example, applying the directive to both `/secret.txt` and `/secret.txt.gz`).

3. Restrict service access:
Restrict network reachability to the BusyBox httpd daemon using local firewall rules if remote access is not required.

Warning: Applying changes to httpd.conf requires restarting or reloading the BusyBox httpd process, which will temporarily terminate active network sessions.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When the HTTP daemon (httpd) has pre-compressed file support enabled, authentication checks are evaluated only against the requested URL path rather than the pre-compressed file being served. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by requesting an uncompressed file path while specifying gzip encoding, bypassing password rules configured specifically for the compressed file. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized information disclosure of sensitive files.

descriptions.description: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel

cna.title: A DCP Set of the IP suite that is refused is still stored

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 copies the IP suite of a DCP Set request to the current and the non-volatile configuration, and starts saving it, before the state of the device is checked. If the request is refused, for example because an Application Relationship is active, the configuration is not restored and is still saved. After a restart the device uses the refused address, and may not answer the controller or may use its address. A host with ADJACENT network access can use this while an Application Relationship is active.

cna.title: Busybox: heap buffer overflow in the tftp client on fallback to the default block size

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Duc Anh Luu for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When the TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) client requests a custom small block size and receives a standard response, it falls back to the default block size without resizing the allocated memory buffer. A malicious TFTP server can exploit this issue by sending standard-sized network packets during a transfer, causing a heap buffer overflow. This flaw allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the application.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse.

The parser appends each chunk to its buffer and compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. It treats a NUL byte as the end of the input, so a NUL within the first max_size bytes keeps it short of the limit. The buffer keeps growing, and incr_skip cannot remove the NUL.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-130

Eclipse Langium versions 3.2.0 through 4.4.0 contain an inefficient algorithmic complexity issue (CWE-407) in the opt-in IndentationAwareTokenBuilder and IndentationAwareLexer. When producing DEDENT tokens, the token builder recomputes line numbers by re-scanning the entire preceding document text. A document whose indentation changes on most lines then takes quadratic time to tokenize. Because tokenization is synchronous, a crafted document of a few hundred kilobytes can block the Node.js event loop for tens of seconds. That causes a DoS for every user served by the same process. Languages built with the DefaultLexer and DefaultTokenBuilder are unaffected.

cna.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via truncated multipart part past the parts limit

descriptions.value: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, when a request reaches the configured limit on the number of multipart parts, each further part is skipped without attaching an error listener to the skipped part stream. If the request body ends in the middle of such a skipped part, the vendored Dicer parser emits an error on that stream, and because nothing is listening Node.js raises an unhandled error event and the process exits. A single crafted unauthenticated request is therefore enough to crash the server. The bug is latent in the parser on its own and was first demonstrated through @fastify/multipart versions 10.1.2 through 10.1.4, which keep feeding the request body to the parser after a limit error, and it affects any consumer that sets a finite parts limit and parses request bodies that can be terminated early. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. There is no complete application level workaround because the crash happens inside the parser before application code runs, though consumers that set a finite parts limit should also attach an error listener to the parser stream.

cna.title: @fastify/multipart vulnerable to arbitrary file write via type confusion in saveRequestFiles()

descriptions.value: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 7.4.0 through 10.1.8, when the plugin is registered with the attachFieldsToBody option, the saveRequestFiles helper treats any object in the parsed request body that carries truthy file and buffer properties as an uploaded file. An unauthenticated client can forge such an object through a plain JSON request or a JSON-typed multipart field, so attacker-chosen bytes are written to the temporary directory while upload hooks and the file count and size limits are skipped, and the saved entry keeps the attacker's filename verbatim instead of being reduced to its basename. Because that filename can contain parent directory segments, applications that use it as a write destination, as the project README example does, are exposed to an arbitrary relative-path file write from a single request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.9, and users should upgrade to 10.1.9 or later. As a workaround, call saveRequestFiles only after confirming the request is multipart, and reduce each returned filename to its basename or validate it against an allowlist before using it as a destination.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag.

With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth.

A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.

descriptions.value: Gitleaks through 8.30.1 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows local users to read scan reports because cmd/root.go creates the --report-path file with os.Create and default permissions. Unless --redact is passed, other local users on shared hosts or CI runners can read plaintext secrets and matching lines to obtain discovered credentials.

descriptions.description: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

cna.title: Relative path traversal in the log export commands in AWS ParallelCluster CLI

descriptions.value: CAPEC-139 Relative Path Traversal

The export-cluster-logs and export-image-logs commands in the AWS ParallelCluster CLI before version 3.16.0 contain a relative path traversal issue. An authenticated remote user with write access to the log export Amazon S3 bucket could use a crafted S3 object key to write files outside the intended export directory on the machine running the command. The written files would have names and content controlled by a third party, and would be created with the privileges of the user running the command.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 3.16.0 or later.

cna.title: Busybox: heap buffer overflow in wget ftp resume when the resume offset exceeds the reported file size

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Seokwoo Jang (AXGATE) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When resuming a download over File Transfer Protocol (FTP), the wget utility fails to verify that the resume offset does not exceed the file size reported by the server, resulting in an integer calculation error. A malicious FTP server or an on-path network attacker can exploit this issue by returning crafted file size metadata, triggering a heap-based buffer overflow with attacker-controlled data. Successful exploitation may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code or crash the application, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

cna.title: Cross-Site Scripting in Kendo UI for jQuery Form Item Hints

descriptions.value: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery Form, the items[].hint option is documented as a string but is rendered as HTML. An attacker who can influence a Form item's hint can cause attacker-controlled markup to execute as JavaScript when a user views the rendered form. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. The first affected version is 2020.2.513; the latest vulnerable version is 2026.3.1015. The issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1111.

cna.title: Phison E12/E18 SSD Controller BootROM Secure Boot Bypass

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Phison E12/E18 SSD Controller BootROM Secure Boot Bypass

descriptions.value: Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attacker to inject persistent boot-patch tuples into the unsigned, CRC-protected flash ID page read by the BootROM. By overwriting a fuse-derived RAM variable via a crafted patch entry using Phison Vendor Specific Commands, an attacker can force CRC-only firmware verification instead of signature checking, enabling an unsigned firmware image to load and creating a persistent controller-level implant that survives firmware reinstallation and operates below the host operating system.

cna.title: Unbounded Memory Retention in QUIC Server for Rejected Streams

descriptions.value:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

cna.title: Masteriyo LMS <= 3.5.1 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via 'file' Parameter

affected.product: Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates

descriptions.value: The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 3.5.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the course importer. The set_post_metas() method  calls maybe_unserialize() on attacker-controlled postmeta string values parsed from the uploaded JSON import file. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP Objects. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that the site has enable_instructor_registration=true AND enable_guest_checkout=true AND at least one purchasable course exists. Install.php sets enable_instructor_registration=false on fresh installs, so this is a non-default configuration. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

A use-after-free vulnerability exists in Samsung Escargot 5.0.2 in the buffer-access paths for ReloadableString and CompressibleString. Internal raw character accessors and the public StringRef::stringBufferAccessData() API did not preserve the lifetime of the underlying buffer while it remained in use. As a result, idle unloading or garbage-collection compression could release the buffer and leave a stale pointer. Subsequent access may cause the process to crash or, under allocation-dependent conditions, expose limited contents of another heap allocation. The issue was addressed by adding buffer-lifetime reference tracking and removing unsafe raw character accessors.

cna.title: Incorrect default permissions on session transcripts and prompt history in Kiro CLI

descriptions.value: CAPEC-1 Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs

Incorrect default file permissions in Kiro CLI (formerly Amazon Q Developer CLI) before version 2.27.0 on macOS and Linux might allow other local users on the same host to read a user's session transcripts and prompt history, including any credentials or source code they contain. The CLI created its local session storage files with permissions that made them readable by all local users.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to Kiro CLI version 2.27.0 or later and launch it once. Users who ran Amazon Q Developer CLI 1.16.0 through 1.19.x should also delete the ~/.aws/amazonq/.cli_bash_history file or restrict it to the owner.

cna.title: Busybox: httpd stack buffer overflow via an "i:" rule in a subdirectory httpd.conf

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Duc Anh Luu for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Prevent untrusted users from creating or modifying configuration files by restricting write permissions on all web root and subdirectory paths served by BusyBox httpd to administrative accounts only:

chmod -R o-w /path/to/webroot

Additionally, ensure the BusyBox httpd process drops elevated privileges by specifying an unprivileged user with the `-u` flag upon execution:

busybox httpd -u nobody

Restarting the daemon is required for process-level flag changes to take effect, which will temporarily terminate active network connections.

Caveats: Running under a non-privileged user account prevents binding directly to privileged ports (below 1024) without additional system capabilities or port forwarding, and restricting directory permissions may interfere with workflows that require unprivileged file uploads.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When the httpd web server processes subdirectory configuration files, an overly long index page name can trigger a stack-based buffer overflow. An attacker with permissions to write to a subdirectory configuration file could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges or cause a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the server process.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox's udhcpc6 DHCPv6 client. cna.title: Apache Commons Codec: NUL bytes in tree entry names cause Git/SWHID identifier collisions (GitIdentifiers class)

descriptions.value:
The GitIdentifiers class in Apache Commons Codec did not reject NUL bytes in tree entry names. Because Git uses a NUL byte to mark the end of each entry name in a tree object, a crafted name could make one tree serialize to the same bytes as a different tree. Two different directory trees could then receive the same Git tree identifier or SWHID.



The impact is limited: common file systems do not allow NUL bytes in file names, so trees built by walking a file system are not affected. Only applications that build trees from names supplied by other sources, such as entries of archive formats that permit NUL bytes in names (e.g. ZIP) or names passed directly to the API, are exposed.



This issue affects Apache Commons Codec: from 1.22.0 before 1.23.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: Integer underflow of the record data length in IODWrite requests

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.

cna.title: SQL Injection in Database Migration via Stored Connector Identifiers in flowintel

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [security] Bind stored connector identifiers during

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] Bind stored connector identifiers during
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The vulnerability is remediated by replacing direct string interpolation of stored database values into SQL queries with parameterized (bound) queries, ensuring that user-supplied or stored data is treated strictly as data rather than executable SQL. Additionally, the NULL handling for identifier fields is corrected to use proper SQL NULL instead of the string literal 'null', preventing both injection and unintended data corruption.
assumptions: The affected version range is inferred from the explicit context (affected_version '0', fixed_version '<=4.0.0'); the exact starting version is not confirmed by the patch itself.
PR:L assumes the attacker can write to the database via an authenticated application role or direct DB access; the specific authentication mechanism is not stated in the patch.
The CVSS impact ratings (VC:H, VI:H, VA:H) assume the database user has broad privileges; if the DB account is highly restricted, impact could be lower.
CAPEC-126 is selected as the closest match; the stored/timed nature of the injection (data planted before migration runs) is a variant not explicitly covered by a more specific CAPEC.
The patch does not indicate whether the migration has already been executed in deployed instances, which would affect real-world exploitability.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In migrations/versions/5cd03995339b_.py, four SQL statements (two SELECT and two UPDATE) are converted from Python f-string interpolation to SQLAlchemy parameterized queries using named bind parameters (:case_id, :instance_id, :ident, :id, :task_id). The NULL identifier handling is changed from assigning the string 'null' to assigning Python None, which SQLAlchemy translates to a proper SQL NULL value.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:L: The migration runs locally on the application server; exploitation requires local access to the database. AC:H: High complexity because the attacker must first write a crafted identifier into the database and then wait for a migration to execute. AT:P: Attack targeting is present; the attacker must specifically craft a malicious SQL payload in the identifier field. PR:L: Low privilege; the attacker needs write access to the database (e.g., an authenticated application user or DB access). UI:N: The migration runs automatically during upgrade; no user interaction is required at trigger time. VC:H, VI:H, VA:H: Successful SQL injection allows arbitrary read, write, and destructive operations on the database. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N: Impact is confined to the local database; no evidence of cross-component or cross-system impact.

capecRationale.rationale: The vulnerability is a textbook SQL injection: attacker-controlled data (stored connector identifiers) is concatenated into SQL statements without sanitization or parameterization. CAPEC-126 is the most direct and specific match. The stored nature of the injection (data planted earlier, executed later during migration) is a variant but still falls squarely within this pattern.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The patch directly replaces f-string interpolation of stored values into SQL with parameterized queries, which is the canonical fix for CWE-89. The commit message explicitly states that stored identifiers were 'interpolated into SQL, allowing expressions to execute,' confirming SQL injection.

Additionally, the NULL handling for identifier fields is corrected to use proper SQL NULL instead of the string literal 'null', preventing both injection and unintended data corruption.

descriptions.value:
A SQL injection vulnerability exists in a database migration script in flowintel.

The migration process reads stored connector identifier values from the database and interpolates them directly into SQL statements without parameterization. An attacker who has previously written a malicious identifier value into the affected tables can cause arbitrary SQL execution when the migration is subsequently run during an application upgrade.

- Requires prior write access to the database to plant a malicious identifier value
- Triggered automatically during a migration or upgrade operation
- Can result in unauthorized data disclosure, modification, or deletion

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.0.0

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str.

A string is decoded through a fixed-size buffer (16 KiB in 4.04), and each time the buffer fills its contents move into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the string is then rejected for a control character, an invalid escape, malformed UTF-8 or the end of the input.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains the decoded part of each rejected string, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

descriptions.description: CWE-401 Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

cna.title: Apache Axis2/C: Out-of-bounds read in the Guththila XML reader wrapper

descriptions.value: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the Guththila XML parser wrapper of Apache Axis2/C. On some malformed XML input the Guththila parser returned a raw input byte in place of an event code, and the AXIOM reader wrapper used that value as an index into a ten-entry lookup table without checking its range, reading heap memory past the end of the table. An unauthenticated client could trigger this by sending a crafted XML request to a server built with Guththila, the default parser, causing the request to be parsed incorrectly or, in some cases, the process to crash. The memory read is not returned to the client. This issue affects Apache Axis2/C: through 2.0.0. The fix is available in commits 23110287924e79d05a5b4712298c355d1f05c606 and f01683ec10e8fddb87279ec9351b3239021223e6 and will be included in the next release.

descriptions.value: The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_urls_in_value function in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

references.name: Streaming request body limit enforced only after an 8 MB read in elixir-grpc grpc_server

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming requests.

The streaming read clause of GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.Handler.info/3 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy/handler.ex) asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read and compares the running total with max_body_size only after the read returns. The gRPC length prefix of a message is not checked before the message is buffered. Each stream can therefore buffer up to one full read beyond the configured limit before it is refused, and many concurrent streams exhaust node memory. Releases before 1.0.6 apply no limit to streaming requests at all.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Large reads

async_read_body/2 asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read on the streaming path, whatever max_body_size is set to.

2. The limit is checked after the read

track_body_bytes/2 adds each returned chunk to a running total and refuses the stream with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED only once the total exceeds max_body_size. By then the whole chunk is in memory.

3. No check on the length prefix

The 5-byte gRPC prefix can declare up to 4 GiB. The server does not compare it with any limit before buffering, so a prefix that declares an oversized message does not stop the read.

4. Result

Each client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming call can make the server hold several megabytes more than the configured limit, and the attacker can open many such calls at once. Before 1.0.6 the streaming path had no limit, and GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.reading_stream/1 buffered the whole body.

references.name: Path bindings ignored for gRPC Content-Types on transcoded routes in elixir-grpc grpc_server

descriptions.value:
Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to make a handler act on a resource other than the one named in the URL of an HTTP-transcoded route, via a request with a gRPC Content-Type.

Only the transcoding clause of GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server.ex, and lib/grpc/server.ex before the package split) applies the route's path bindings to the request message. The Cowboy handler picks that clause from the request Content-Type, not from the route. A request to a transcoded URL with application/grpc or application/grpc-web is decoded from the body alone, so every path-bound field takes its value from the body. A gateway, proxy rule or WAF that authorizes on the URL path sees one resource while the handler receives another.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. The header selects the clause

The Cowboy handler derives the access mode from the request Content-Type. application/json selects :http_transcoding, application/grpc selects :grpc and application/grpc-web+proto selects :grpcweb. The router still matches the transcoded URL template and extracts its path bindings.

2. Bindings are applied in one clause only

GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 reads the bindings with adapter.get_bindings/1 and merges them through GRPC.Server.Transcode.map_request/5 only in the :http_transcoding clause. The unary and request-streaming clauses decode the body alone with the selected codec. GRPC.Codec.Proto is in the default codecs of every server, so application/grpc is always accepted.

3. The HTTP/1.1 guard never matches

resolve_access_mode/3 has a clause that forces transcoding for HTTP/1.1 requests. It matches the version as the binary "HTTP/1.1", while Cowboy stores the version as an atom, so the clause never applies and the request works over plain HTTP/1.1.

4. Result

A request to /v1/messages/alice with Content-Type: application/grpc and a message that sets name to victim reaches the handler with name set to victim. With an empty message the field is empty: the path binding is never consulted.

cna.title: Apache APISIX: Multi-auth preserves client-supplied Wolf identity headers

descriptions.value:
Authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



On a route where multi-auth falls back from wolf-rbac to another successful authenticator, client-supplied Wolf identity headers can remain in the request. A downstream service that relies on those documented headers may therefore receive an identity that was not established by the successful authenticator.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.8.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.

Similar can happen when forward-auth is configured with allow_degradation: true, and the auth service is unavailable.

This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.18.0 through 3.19.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: IBM1390/IBM1399 encoders may read past input

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of buffer however does not account for this, which may result in a buffer overread if the following code point has less than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 finds the RPC session of a received PDU by its activity UUID only, and a reject, fault or cancel PDU for the session aborts the Application Relationship, without checking that the PDU is the answer to a call of the device or where it comes from. cna.title: `http.cookiejar` applies expired `Set-Cookie` to cookie store before policy validation

descriptions.value:
http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response carried an
already expired Set-Cookie header for it, using the Domain and Path
attributes from the header without consulting the cookie policy. A server
could therefore delete cookies belonging to other domains from a shared
cookie jar, such as the one used by urllib's HTTPCookieProcessor. The fix
consults the cookie policy before an expired cookie may delete an existing
one, as required by RFC 6265 section 5.3.

cna.title: mouse07410/asn1c: 1-byte Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in `INTEGER_decode_oer` via Malformed OER Payload

descriptions.value: mouse07410/asn1c is an ASN.1 compiler. In 1.4 and earlier, a memory safety vulnerability was identified in the OER decoding skeleton files generated by asn1c (specifically INTEGER_oer.c). When parsing a maliciously crafted, zero-length OER payload for a variable-length, non-negative INTEGER type, the decoder fails to validate the required bytes before extracting the Most Significant Bit (MSB). This forces a precise 1-byte Heap Out-of-Bounds (OOB) Read. Because asn1c generated code is primarily deployed to parse untrusted network inputs (such as V2X network protocols, 5G telecom headers, or X.509 certificates), when the decoder processes untrusted network-originated input, a remote attacker can exploit this to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or trigger incorrect integer interpretation in downstream applications (e.g., protocol state poisoning or logic bypass).

cna.title: Goobi viewer: Unauthenticated Solr Streaming Expression Proxy

descriptions.value: The Goobi viewer is a web application that allows digitised material to be displayed in a web browser. From 4.8.0 to before 26.04.1, the Goobi viewer REST endpoint POST /api/v1/index/stream accepted an arbitrary Solr streaming expression from unauthenticated network clients and forwarded it to the backend Solr server without restriction. An attacker could read the complete Solr index and, in default Solr deployments, also modify or delete indexed records. This vulnerability is fixed in 26.04.1.

descriptions.value: Nextcloud is an open source content collaboration platform. From versions 1.15.0 to before 1.15.4, 1.16.0 to before 1.16.3, 1.17.0 to before 1.17.1, and 1.18.0 to before 1.18.1, a malicious user with access to an end-to-end encrypted files drop link was able to also drop files into other end-to-end encrypted folders of the share owner. Reading and modifying of other files was not possible. This issue has been patched in versions 1.15.4, 1.16.3, 1.17.1, 1.18.1, and 2.0.0-rc.7.

cna.title: OpenTelemetry-Go's Schema ParseFile leaks file descriptors on each parse

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. Prior to version 0.0.17, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/schema/v1.0` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/schema/v1.1` leaks one file descriptor on each successful `ParseFile` call. `ParseFile` opens the schema file and passes it to `Parse` without closing it; repeated parsing in a long-running process can exhaust the process file descriptor limit and cause denial of service. Exploitation depends on a consuming application exposing repeated schema parsing to an attacker-controlled path. Version 0.0.17 contains a patch for the issue.

cna.title: Suricata dnp3: unbounded reassembly can lead to resource exhaustion

descriptions.value: Suricata is a network Intrusion Detection System, Intrusion Prevention System and Network Security Monitoring engine. Prior to versions 7.0.16 and 8.0.5, DNP3 reassembly could buffer data without sufficient parser-level bounds. Crafted DNP3 traffic may cause Suricata to consume excessive memory, potentially resulting in denial of service. Versions 7.0.16 and 8.0.5 contain a fix. As a workaround, disable DNP3 (which is not enabled by default) if it is not needed, and/or define a limited `stream.reassembly.depth` (0 or absent is unlimited).

cna.title: drm/amdkfd: Fix watch_id bounds checking in debug address watch v2

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The vulnerability is reached only through an ioctl (AMDKFD_IOC_DBG_TRAP) on the local /dev/kfd device node; there is no network or remote path.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls both the allocation of a watch point and the crafted watch_id; the negative-shift behavior is deterministic on x86, so the out-of-bounds write is triggered reliably and repeatably.
PR:L - The ioctl has flags=0 with no capability check, and self-debugging (target==p) is permitted, so any unprivileged local user with access to the GPU device node (/dev/kfd) can reach the bug; no root/CAP_SYS_ADMIN is required.
UI:N - The attacking process performs the enable/allocate/clear sequence entirely on its own; no action by another user is needed.
S:U - The out-of-bounds write corrupts kernel memory within the same kernel security authority; it does not cross into a separate authority such as a hypervisor or IOMMU boundary.
C:H - The bug is a kernel out-of-bounds write (memory corruption) that can be groomed to overwrite adjacent kernel structures (e.g., size/pointer fields), which can be leveraged to enable information disclosure.
I:H - Attacker-influenced out-of-bounds write of a 32-bit value into kernel memory at a controllable offset is a direct kernel memory-corruption/write primitive.
A:H - The out-of-bounds write into unmapped or critical kernel memory readily causes a kernel oops/panic, producing a denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdkfd: Fix watch_id bounds checking in debug address watch v2

The address watch clear code receives watch_id as an unsigned value
(u32), but some helper functions were using a signed int and checked
bits by shifting with watch_id.

If a very large watch_id is passed from userspace, it can be converted
to a negative value.  This can cause invalid shifts and may access
memory outside the watch_points array.

drm/amdkfd: Fix watch_id bounds checking in debug address watch v2

Fix this by checking that watch_id is within MAX_WATCH_ADDRESSES before
using it.  Also use BIT(watch_id) to test and clear bits safely.

This keeps the behavior unchanged for valid watch IDs and avoids
undefined behavior for invalid ones.

Fixes the below:
drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/../amdkfd/kfd_debug.c:448
kfd_dbg_trap_clear_dev_address_watch() error: buffer overflow
'pdd->watch_points' 4 <= u32max user_rl='0-3,2147483648-u32max' uncapped

drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/../amdkfd/kfd_debug.c
    433 int kfd_dbg_trap_clear_dev_address_watch(struct kfd_process_device *pdd,
    434                                         uint32_t watch_id)
    435 {
    436         int r;
    437
    438         if (!kfd_dbg_owns_dev_watch_id(pdd, watch_id))

kfd_dbg_owns_dev_watch_id() doesn't check for negative values so if
watch_id is larger than INT_MAX it leads to a buffer overflow.
(Negative shifts are undefined).

    439                 return -EINVAL;
    440
    441         if (!pdd->dev->kfd->shared_resources.enable_mes) {
    442                 r = debug_lock_and_unmap(pdd->dev->dqm);
    443                 if (r)
    444                         return r;
    445         }
    446
    447         amdgpu_gfx_off_ctrl(pdd->dev->adev, false);
--> 448         pdd->watch_points[watch_id] = pdd->dev->kfd2kgd->clear_address_watch(
    449                                                         pdd->dev->adev,
    450                                                         watch_id);

v2: (as per, Jonathan Kim)
 - Add early watch_id >= MAX_WATCH_ADDRESSES validation in the set path to
   match the clear path.
 - Drop the redundant bounds check in kfd_dbg_owns_dev_watch_id().

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/uverbs: Validate wqe_size before using it in ib_uverbs_post_send

ib_uverbs_post_send() uses cmd.wqe_size from userspace without any
validation before passing it to kmalloc() and using the allocated
buffer as struct ib_uverbs_send_wr.

If a user provides a small wqe_size value (e.g., 1), kmalloc() will
succeed, but subsequent accesses to user_wr->opcode, user_wr->num_sge,
and other fields will read beyond the allocated buffer, resulting in
an out-of-bounds read from kernel heap memory. This could potentially
leak sensitive kernel information to userspace.

Additionally, providing an excessively large wqe_size can trigger a
WARNING in the memory allocation path, as reported by syzkaller.

This is inconsistent with ib_uverbs_unmarshall_recv() which properly
validates that wqe_size >= sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_recv_wr) before
proceeding.

Add the same validation for ib_uverbs_post_send() to ensure wqe_size
is at least sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr).

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The vulnerable code is reached via write() on the local RDMA uverbs character device (/dev/infiniband/uverbs*) dispatched through UAPI_DEF_WRITE_IO; it is not reachable over any network.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls cmd.wqe_size and can reliably trigger the OOB read by simply setting wqe_size=1 (or the WARN with a huge value); no uncontrolled conditions are involved.
PR:L - An unprivileged local user with access to the RDMA uverbs device (the normal case on RDMA-enabled systems, and obtainable via Soft-RoCE) can open a context, create a QP, and issue POST_SEND; no real-root privilege is required.
UI:N - The command is issued directly by the attacker via a syscall; no action by any other user is needed.
S:U - The OOB read and resulting impact remain within the kernel's own security authority; no crossing of a security boundary (VM/IOMMU/sandbox) occurs.
C:H - The bug reads ~48 bytes of kernel heap memory beyond the undersized allocation, and the leaked values (e.g. wr_id) are returned to userspace via completion polling, giving a repeatable kernel-heap information disclosure.
I:N - The defect is purely an out-of-bounds read; num_sge is bounded by the sge_count check, so no kernel memory is modified and there is no write primitive.
A:H - An excessively large wqe_size triggers a WARNING in the allocator (syzkaller-reported), which becomes a kernel panic under the common panic_on_warn hardening, causing denial of service.

Symfony: OidcTokenHandler Accepts JWTs Missing aud/iss/exp Claims

descriptions.value: Symfony is a PHP framework for web and console applications and a set of reusable PHP components. Prior to 6.4.40, 7.4.12, and 8.0.12, OidcTokenHandler::verifyClaims() registered audience (aud), issuer (iss), and expiry (exp) checkers but did not pass the mandatory claims list to ClaimCheckerManager::check(), so a validly signed JWT that omitted those claims could pass verification. cna.title: SiYuan: Bazaar marketplace renders unescaped package `name` and `version` metadata, allowing stored XSS and Electron code execution

descriptions.value: SiYuan is an open-source personal knowledge management system. Prior to 3.7.0, SiYuan's Bazaar (community marketplace) renders the name and version fields of a package's plugin.json (and the equivalent theme.json / template.json / widget.json / icon.json) into the Settings → Marketplace UI without HTML escaping. The kernel-side helper sanitizePackageDisplayStrings in kernel/bazaar/package.go HTML-escapes only Author, DisplayName, and Description — Name and Version flow through to the renderer raw. The frontend at app/src/config/bazaar.ts substitutes them into HTML template strings via ${item.preferredName} / ${data.name} / v${data.version} and assigns the result to innerHTML. As a consequence, malicious HTML in either field is parsed and executed when a user opens the marketplace tab. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.7.0.

cna.title: Termix Vulnerable to Arbitrary Command Execution in File Manager

descriptions.value: Termix is a web-based server management platform with SSH terminal, tunneling, and file editing capabilities. Prior to version 2.3.2, the GET /ssh/file_manager/ssh/resolvePath endpoint in the Termix File Manager component unsafely processes the path parameter and embeds it into a shell command executed over the active SSH session. Because the user-controlled value is placed inside double quotes and only double quotes are escaped, shell command substitution syntax such as $(...) is still interpreted by the remote shell. Version 2.3.2 fixes the issue.
